title: Design an Expense-Sharing App (Splitwise)
prompt: Design the object model for an expense-sharing application like Splitwise. Users create groups, add expenses that are split among members (equally, by exact amounts, or by percentage), and the app tracks who owes whom. Design the core classes, their relationships, and the key methods. Focus on the class design and APIs, not the distributed backend. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: Classic money-domain OOD — pluggable split strategies, balance sheets, and a settle-up debt-simplification graph.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Separates functional (add expense, multiple split types, group vs 1:1, balances, settle up) from non-functional (money correctness, no lost pennies, auditability, concurrency on shared balances).

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Identifies User, Group, Expense, Split, Transaction/Settlement, and a Balance/ledger abstraction — not one god class.

rubric.label: Class design & responsibilities
rubric.description: Each class has a single clear responsibility; money is a first-class type (cents/BigDecimal), not float; Split is abstracted from Expense.

rubric.label: Relationships & cardinality
rubric.description: Group has many Users; Expense has one payer and many Splits; Split references a User and a share; BalanceSheet aggregates directed debts. Composition vs association reasoned.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: Strategy for split calculation (Equal/Exact/Percent), Factory for creating splits from a request, optionally Observer for balance updates/notifications.

rubric.label: SOLID / OCP
rubric.description: Adding a new split type (e.g. by shares/adjustment) requires no change to Expense — open for extension. Validation lives with the strategy.

rubric.label: API / method design
rubric.description: addExpense, getBalances(user), getGroupBalances(group), settleUp(from,to,amount), simplifyDebts(group) with clear signatures and return types.

rubric.label: Edge cases & correctness
rubric.description: Penny rounding on unequal splits, percentages must sum to 100, exact shares must sum to total, payer in split, self-settlement, negative/zero amounts, currency mismatch.

rubric.label: Concurrency
rubric.description: Two expenses mutating the same pair's balance concurrently; idempotent expense creation; locking or per-account serialization / event log.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: Multi-currency, recurring expenses, debt simplification, comments/attachments added without reshaping the core model.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Drives clarification, narrates the class diagram, states tradeoffs, reasons aloud about correctness.

functional_requirements: Create users and groups; add/remove members
Add an expense: a payer, a total amount, and a set of participants
Support split types: EQUAL, EXACT (per-person amounts), PERCENT
Compute each user's net balance overall and per group (who owes whom)
Settle up: record a payment from one user to another that reduces debt
Optionally simplify debts within a group to minimize number of transactions
nonfunctional_requirements: Monetary correctness — no lost or created pennies across a split
Deterministic, auditable balance changes (append-only ledger friendly)
Consistency of shared balances under concurrent expense creation
Extensible to new split strategies and multi-currency without core rewrites
clarifying_questions: One currency or multi-currency? If multi, do we convert or keep per-currency balances?
Which split types must we support at launch — equal, exact, percent, shares?
Is the payer always a single user, or can multiple users pay for one expense?
Do balances live per-group only, or is there a global cross-group net balance per pair?
Do we need debt simplification (minimize transactions) or literal pairwise debts?
Do we need an audit trail / edit history for expenses?

core_classes.name: Group
core_classes.responsibility: A named set of users that share expenses; scopes a BalanceSheet.

core_classes.name: Money
core_classes.responsibility: Value type for currency amounts; avoids float errors.

core_classes.name: Expense
core_classes.responsibility: One shared cost: who paid, total, and how it splits.

core_classes.name: Split
core_classes.responsibility: One participant's owed share of an expense.

core_classes.name: SplitStrategy
core_classes.responsibility: Abstract algorithm that turns an expense total + inputs into per-user Splits and validates them.
key_methods: computeSplits(Money total, List<User> participants, Object params) -> List<Split>

core_classes.name: EqualSplit / ExactSplit / PercentSplit
core_classes.responsibility: Concrete strategies; EqualSplit distributes remainder pennies deterministically, ExactSplit asserts shares sum to total, PercentSplit asserts percentages sum to 100.

core_classes.name: BalanceSheet
core_classes.responsibility: Aggregates directed pairwise debts (a owes b) from expenses and settlements.

core_classes.name: Settlement
core_classes.responsibility: A recorded payment from one user to another reducing debt.

core_classes.name: ExpenseService
core_classes.responsibility: Application service: creates expenses via a SplitFactory, updates the BalanceSheet, emits events.

relationships: Group *— composed of —* User (many-to-many via membership); Group owns its Expenses (composition) and one BalanceSheet (composition).
Expense has exactly one payer (User, association) and one SplitStrategy (strategy reference); Expense composes many Split objects.
Split associates to a User and holds a Money share.
BalanceSheet is derived from the ordered stream of Expenses + Settlements; it is aggregation/projection, not source of truth.
ExpenseService depends on SplitFactory (creates strategies) and on a repository abstraction (DIP).

design_patterns.why: Split math varies independently of Expense; new split types plug in without touching Expense (OCP).

design_patterns.where: SplitFactory maps a request's split type + params to a concrete strategy
design_patterns.why: Centralizes creation and validation of strategies; callers stay decoupled from concrete classes.
Encapsulates currency + integer minor-units and safe arithmetic incl. remainder allocation; forbids float bugs.

design_patterns.where: BalanceSheet notifies NotificationService / activity feed on change
design_patterns.why: Decouples side effects (notify, feed) from the core balance update.

apis: addExpense(groupId, paidBy, amount, splitType, participants, params) -> Expense
state_transitions: Expense: DRAFT -> VALIDATED (splits sum to total) -> RECORDED (applied to BalanceSheet). An edited expense reverses its prior effect then re-applies.
Debt for a pair: reduced by Settlements until zero; can flip sign if the debtor overpays.
edge_cases: EQUAL split of $10 among 3 → 3.34/3.33/3.33; remainder pennies allocated deterministically so shares sum exactly to total
EXACT split whose parts don't sum to the total → reject
PERCENT split whose percentages don't sum to 100 → reject
Payer is also a participant → their own share is netted out, not owed to themselves
Zero or negative expense amount → reject
Settle-up amount greater than outstanding debt → either reject or create reverse credit; must be explicit
Currency mismatch between expense and group/settlement → reject or convert per policy
Removing a member who still has non-zero balance → block or require settle-up first
concurrency: Two expenses touching the same user pair concurrently — serialize per (user,user) key or per group with a lock, or make BalanceSheet an append-only event log reduced on read
Idempotency: dedupe addExpense by a client-supplied requestId to survive retries
If balances are cached, invalidate/recompute atomically with the ledger write
Prefer immutable Expense/Settlement records + recompute over in-place mutation to keep concurrency reasoning simple
extensibility: New split type SharesSplit / AdjustmentSplit → add a strategy, register in factory, no Expense change
Multi-currency → Money already carries currency; add balances per currency or an FX conversion policy
Recurring expenses → a Scheduler that emits Expenses on a cadence
Comments, receipts/attachments → separate entities associated to Expense
Debt simplification → an algorithm over BalanceSheet, swappable

deep_dives.probe: $100 split equally three ways. Walk me through exactly how Money.allocate distributes the leftover cent so the shares sum back to $100. Is it deterministic across runs?
Show the SplitStrategy interface and how ExactSplit vs PercentSplit validate their inputs. Where does the 'percentages must sum to 100' rule live, and why there?
In a group, A owes B $10 and B owes C $10. How do you minimize transactions to a single A→C $10? Model this as a graph and describe the algorithm and its cost.
Is BalanceSheet the source of truth or a projection of an expense/settlement log? What does each choice buy you for auditing and concurrency?
Why not use double for amounts? What type do you use and how does it interact with currency?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions float or double for money
followup_bank.question: Floating point for currency will drift. What type do you use for amounts, and how do you handle the leftover cent in an uneven split?
Add a fourth split type — by shares (2:1:1). How much of your code changes? If Expense changes, your design isn't open/closed.
Is the balance stored and mutated, or derived from a log of expenses and settlements? Defend it against concurrent edits.
What if someone settles more than they owe? How does the model represent the resulting credit?
How do you minimize the number of settle-up transactions in a group? What's the graph formulation?

tradeoffs: Stored balances (fast reads) vs derived-from-log balances (auditable, concurrency-friendly, slower reads)
Literal pairwise debts (transparent) vs simplified debts (fewer payments, less obvious provenance)
Per-group balances (simple) vs global net balances across groups (nicer UX, harder consistency)
Strategy per split type (clean OCP) vs a single parameterized method (less indirection, worse extensibility)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer models Money as a value type over integer minor units with safe allocation, extracts split math into a SplitStrategy hierarchy (Equal/Exact/Percent) created by a SplitFactory so new split types obey OCP, keeps Expense as a payer + total + list of Splits, and treats BalanceSheet as a projection of an append-only stream of Expenses and Settlements. It nails penny-rounding determinism, validates that exact shares sum to the total and percentages to 100, nets the payer out of their own share, and reasons about per-pair concurrency via serialization or an event log. Senior signal: proposing debt simplification as a graph problem and defending balances-as-projection for auditability.

interviewer_notes: Let them scope split types and currency first. The core signal is whether split logic is a Strategy separate from Expense — if they hardcode if/else on split type inside Expense, push with the 'add a 4th split type' follow-up. Force the penny-rounding conversation; a senior candidate raises it unprompted. If they use double for money, interrupt immediately. Reserve time for balances-as-projection vs stored, and for debt simplification as a stretch. Concurrency matters at senior level: ask how two simultaneous expenses on the same pair stay consistent.
